statement: The function returns a result r and r equals the number of integers x such that 1 <= x <= n and x is good. For a positive integer x, write its decimal representation without leading zeros as the digit sequence a_0 a_1 ... a_{k-1}, where a_0 is the most significant digit. Then x is good if and only if: (1) every a_i belongs to {0,1,2,5,6,8,9}; and (2) with rot(0)=0, rot(1)=1, rot(2)=5, rot(5)=2, rot(6)=9, rot(8)=8, rot(9)=6, the digit sequence rot(a_0) rot(a_1) ... rot(a_{k-1}), kept in the same order with no reversal, denotes a decimal integer different from x.
preconditions: n is an I64 value with 1 <= n <= 10000.

statement: The function returns a result r and does not fail: no arithmetic overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic occurs for any n satisfying the precondition.
preconditions: n is an I64 value with 1 <= n <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r <= n.
preconditions: n is an I64 value with 1 <= n <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if n = 1.
preconditions: n is an I64 value with 1 <= n <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r_n on input n and a result r_m on input m, r_n <= r_m.
preconditions: n and m are I64 values with 1 <= n <= m <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r_n on input n and a result r_{n+1} on input n+1, if n+1 is good (meaning every decimal digit of n+1 is in {0,1,2,5,6,8,9} and at least one decimal digit of n+1 is in {2,5,6,9}), then r_{n+1} = r_n + 1.
preconditions: n is an I64 value with 1 <= n < 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r_n on input n and a result r_{n+1} on input n+1, if n+1 is not good (meaning either some decimal digit of n+1 is outside {0,1,2,5,6,8,9}, or no decimal digit of n+1 is in {2,5,6,9}), then r_{n+1} = r_n.
preconditions: n is an I64 value with 1 <= n < 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r > 0 if and only if there exists an integer x with 1 <= x <= n such that x is good (every decimal digit of x is in {0,1,2,5,6,8,9} and at least one decimal digit of x is in {2,5,6,9}).
preconditions: n is an I64 value with 1 <= n <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is at least the number of elements of the set {2,5,6,9} that are less than or equal to n.
preconditions: n is an I64 value with 1 <= n <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = A(n) - B(n), where A(n) is the number of integers x with 1 <= x <= n whose decimal digits all belong to {0,1,2,5,6,8,9}, and B(n) is the number of integers x with 1 <= x <= n whose decimal digits all belong to {0,1,8}.
preconditions: n is an I64 value with 1 <= n <= 10000.
